NextItNet uses residual stacks of dilated causal convolutions to capture short- and long-range item dependencies without pooling. For stride-one convolution layers, the theoretical receptive-field span is R = 1 + Σ(kℓ−1)dℓ, counting every convolution in each block. This architectural calculation suggests a useful diagnostic: perturb history at increasing distances from the readout and compare observed sensitivity with reachable positions. Changes outside that field warrant checking normalization, pooling or other cross-position operations. [Original NextItNet paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf)

Recent research supports measuring ranking sensitivity alongside accuracy. A 2024 study found strong dependence on recent interactions and used Rank List Sensitivity to expose changes obscured by aggregate accuracy; another found weak sequential structure in several popular datasets through shuffling experiments. RecSys 2025 work further distinguishes user-order patterns from item-availability effects using constrained shuffling. These findings motivate controls rather than assuming every shuffle effect represents intent. [Missing-input robustness, 2024](https://iris.uniroma1.it/bitstream/11573/1740238/1/Siciliano_Robust-Training_2024.pdf), [Sequential-structure analysis, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008), [Constrained shuffling, 2025](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748042)

Practical probe proposal: freeze each trained NextItNet; compare original histories with valid-item shuffles that preserve the final item, old-prefix removal, and matched-size recent-event ablations. Keep candidates fixed; report paired HR@10 changes, top-10 overlap and rank displacement by history length and perturbation distance. Reapply left padding consistently and read the final nonpadding position, never count−1. Check causality by changing positions after t and verifying features at t remain unchanged in evaluation mode. These are proposed implementation checks and sensitivity measurements; they cannot establish latent intent or preference drift.
